function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order a cake—whether you’re looking for something local, a specialty dessert, or a nationwide delivery service. | Category | What to Look For | Typical Options | Tips | |----------|------------------|-----------------|------| | **Local Bakeries** | Fresh, custom‑made cakes; often have seasonal specials | - Your neighborhood bakery
- Artisan shops on Main St.
- Specialty pastry shops (e.g., “The Cake Spot”) | • Call ahead to confirm availability and delivery hours.
• Ask about custom designs, flavors, and dietary restrictions (gluten‑free, vegan, nut‑free).
• Check their website or Instagram for photos of past orders. | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | Wide selection from multiple vendors; convenient ordering & tracking | - **Instacart** (partnered local stores)
- **Amazon Fresh** (some regions)
- **Postmates** (in select cities) | • These services usually deliver within 1–3 hours.
• Prices include delivery fees; compare total cost. | | **National Chains** | Consistent quality; often offer nationwide shipping | - **Baker’s Dozen** (specialty cakes)
- **Cake Boss** (custom wedding cakes)
- **Dunkin’ Donuts** (quick delivery) | • Great for large events (weddings, corporate parties).
• Many chains allow online customization and pre‑order. | | **Specialty Online Stores** | Gourmet, niche flavors, or themed cakes | - **Goldbelly** (regional specialties shipped nationwide)
- **Etsy** (hand‑crafted cakes from independent bakers)
- **Tartine Bakery** (online ordering for pickup) | • Ideal for unique flavors (lavender honey, matcha, etc.).
• Shipping times vary; check estimated arrival dates. | | **Catering Services** | Full event packages (cake + tableware + staff) | - Local catering companies
- Corporate catering firms | • Good for large parties; they handle setup and cleanup.
• Ask for sample tastings if possible. | ### How to Choose the Right Option 1. **Determine the Occasion** * Small gathering → local bakery or online platform.
* Wedding or large celebration → national chain or catering service. 2. **Check Reviews & Ratings** * Use Google Maps, Yelp, or Trustpilot to see recent customer feedback.
* Look for photos of actual cakes delivered to gauge quality. 3. **Ask About Customization** * Most bakeries can accommodate special designs, dietary needs, or flavor requests.
* Confirm the turnaround time for custom orders. 4. **Delivery Logistics** * Verify delivery windows, minimum order amounts, and whether the vendor offers same‑day delivery.
* Some services require a deposit or full payment upfront. 5. **Budget** * Local bakeries may charge a delivery fee but often offer better value for fresh, handmade cakes.
* National chains might have higher prices but guarantee brand consistency. ### Quick Order Checklist - [ ] Decide on cake size & flavor.
- [ ] Pick a vendor (local vs. online).
- [ ] Place order at least 24–48 hrs in advance (or earlier for custom designs).
- [ ] Confirm delivery address, time slot, and contact details.
- [ ] Pay securely (most sites accept credit cards or PayPal).
- [ ] Receive confirmation email with tracking info (if applicable).
--- #### Example Order Flow (Using an Online Platform) 1. **Open the app** (Instacart, Amazon Fresh). 2. **Search “cake”** in your city. 3. **Filter by price, rating, or dietary preference**. 4. **Add to cart** and proceed to checkout. 5. **Choose delivery time** (often 1–3 hrs). 6. **Pay** and receive a confirmation. If you let me know your city or specific preferences (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free, chocolate lover), I can narrow down the best local bakeries or online options for you!
